subject: geography
title: Tectonic Hazards Adventure: Case Studies
welcome_lead: Tohoku vs Haiti — why do similar quakes have such different impacts? Time for case studies.
meta_desc: GCSE Geography Tectonic Hazards case studies — Tohoku 2011, Haiti 2010, HIC vs LIC.
final_note: You compared a HIC and LIC earthquake and learned about monitoring, prediction and planning.

concepts.def: Damage caused directly by the shaking itself

walkthroughs.body_html:
Magnitude 9.0 quake offshore triggered a 40m tsunami.

Around 15,900 deaths — mostly from the tsunami, not the shaking. Earthquake-resistant buildings saved thousands. The Fukushima nuclear meltdown was a secondary effect.

Magnitude 7.0 quake near Port-au-Prince — far smaller than Tohoku.

Yet around 230,000 deaths. Poor building quality, no early warning, weak emergency response. A cholera outbreak followed — a deadly secondary effect.

Monitoring: seismometers track tremors; GPS tracks plate movement.

Protection: cross-bracing, base isolators, deep foundations.

Preparation: drills (Japan's Disaster Prevention Day), hazard maps, emergency kits.

mcqs.q: Which is a SECONDARY effect of the 2011 Tohoku earthquake?
options: Buildings collapsing from shaking
The Fukushima nuclear meltdown
Roads cracking
Initial ground rupture

mcqs.q: Why did Haiti 2010 cause far more deaths than Tohoku 2011 despite being a smaller quake?
options: Haiti was closer to the equator
Poor building quality and weak response in an LIC
Haiti has more volcanoes
Tohoku had no tsunami

mcqs.q: Why do earthquakes typically cause more deaths in LICs than HICs?
options: HICs never have earthquake deaths because of advanced technology.
Primary effects happen first and secondary effects happen the next day.
LICs have more earthquake deaths because more earthquakes happen there.
LICs often have poorly enforced building codes, weak emergency response, dense informal housing and limited preparedness — not because the earthquakes are stronger.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary effects of an earthquake?
options: Primary effects are the worst effects and secondary effects are minor.
Primary effects occur immediately as a direct result of shaking (building collapse, deaths); secondary effects follow afterwards (fires, tsunamis, disease, homelessness).
All earthquakes of magnitude 7 cause the same damage everywhere.
Primary effects happen first and secondary effects happen the next day.

mcqs.q: Why do earthquakes of similar magnitude cause different amounts of damage?
options: All earthquakes of magnitude 7 cause the same damage everywhere.
Damage depends on depth, distance from population, building quality, ground type (liquefaction risk), time of day, and emergency preparedness — not just magnitude.
Bigger magnitude always means more deaths.
Primary effects happen first and secondary effects happen the next day.
